content: 1. Review the existing mechanisms for reporting, investigating, assessing causality, classifying, and managing Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFIs) and Adverse Events of Special Interest (AESIs). Ensure these systems are up-to-date and effective. 2. Identify and establish, if not already available, national and sub-national committees responsible for reviewing and classifying AEFI cases. Define their composition, roles, and activity timelines. 3. Analyze gaps and challenges in AEFI surveillance for new pandemic vaccines, incorporating lessons learned from previous pandemic vaccine rollouts. 4. Map the roles and responsibilities of stakeholders and partners, including regional centers for disease control, to facilitate regional and global situation analysis. 5. Evaluate the current surveillance systems for vaccine-preventable diseases and determine how they can be extended or enhanced for use during a pandemic. 6. Define the critical data points to be collected to inform decision-making throughout the pandemic vaccination campaign. 7. Establish a mechanism to standardize clinical specimen collection and map accredited laboratories for specimen testing. 8. Plan the type of surveillance to be conducted during the pandemic, such as sentinel site surveillance, case-based surveillance, or community surveillance. Specify details like the number of sites and target age or risk groups for sentinel surveillance. 9. Assess the budgetary implications and identify funding sources for surveillance activities. 10. Ensure a mechanism is in place for reporting surveillance data to the World Health Organization (WHO) to understand disease epidemiology and vaccine effectiveness. 11. Develop plans for intra-action reviews to incorporate lessons learned and strengthen vaccination activities. 12. Define a timeline, mechanism, and key areas for post-introduction evaluation of pandemic vaccination efforts. 13. Identify funding needs for preparedness and response activities, breaking down costs into specific components. 14. Outline funding sources for the required budget, including phase-wise budgetary requirements. 15. Map potential donors and engage them regularly, including during simulation exercises. 16. Establish a monitoring system for funding to track preparedness activities and reassess funding needs as necessary. 17. Ensure high-level political support to secure vaccination funding and enable coordination among multi-sectoral stakeholders. 18. Coordinate closely with domestic and international partners and donors to ensure timely procurement of adequate vaccine supplies. 19. Engage private sector providers, village health teams, and community leaders in planning and coordination committees. 20. Conduct regular meetings between national, provincial, and district-level management groups to identify technical assistance and financing needs at sub-national levels. 21. Develop district micro-plans to allocate resources effectively and improve service delivery. 22. Use evidence-based public health goals to guide pandemic response, considering key population groups and the evolving pandemic context. 23. In supply-constrained environments, consider vaccine allocation approaches that synergize with other medical countermeasures. 24. Design multi-faceted vaccination strategies informed by past experiences with medical product deployment in emergencies. 25. Implement rapid monitoring and feedback mechanisms to ensure equitable vaccine access and minimize wastage. 26. Strengthen National Regulatory Authorities (NRAs) to enable fast-tracking of regulatory approvals, issuing emergency use authorizations, and facilitating rapid vaccine clearance upon arrival. 27. Develop flexible and agile vaccine delivery strategies that maintain service quality and adapt to emerging evidence. 28. Include provisions for hard-to-reach populations, such as refugees, internally displaced persons, and those in correctional facilities or military camps. 29. Plan for potential disruptions due to pandemic-related travel restrictions. 30. Engage private facilities to increase the availability of vaccination sites. 31. Maintain operational outreach and mobile vaccination sites, especially for delivering second doses in hard-to-reach areas. 32. Leverage ongoing public health programs to identify and mobilize key populations for vaccination. 33. Use integrated IT platforms for registration, tracking, and issuing vaccination certificates, as well as monitoring cold chain status and vaccine availability. 34. Employ a combination of vaccine delivery strategies, such as drones for remote areas, mobile vans for sparsely populated regions, and newly established vaccination sites in diverse locations. 35. Optimize supply chain operations by preparing guidelines and procedures for operational, supply chain, and waste management planning. 36. Select vaccines based on cold chain requirements and vial size to ensure proper storage and transport. 37. Conduct periodic nationwide assessments of cold chain storage capacities to identify additional equipment needs. 38. Identify funding sources for acquiring ultra-cold chain equipment, refrigerated trucks, and other necessary supplies. 39. Establish strategic partnerships with couriers, airlines, and security forces for secure vaccine distribution. 40. Implement real-time monitoring of vaccine stocks to enable need-based redistribution and reduce wastage. 41. Adopt best practices for vaccines with short expiry dates, such as monitoring expiry and batch releases, rapid vaccination, and redistributing extra doses. 42. Ensure a sufficient, trained, and supported workforce by developing training plans for all staff and volunteers involved in vaccination activities. 43. Conduct training through various modalities, including face-to-face, on-the-job, and virtual environments. 44. Provide refresher and continuous training for vaccination staff to ensure they have the most up-to-date information. 45. Implement mass training and training of trainers before national vaccination campaigns. 46. Ensure the availability of training platforms for rapid training in addition to in-person and cascaded training models. 47. Create a working plan to provide adequate supportive supervision for front-line health workers. 48. Conduct simulation exercises to maintain and test capabilities. 49. Enhance digital literacy in the community to support vaccination efforts. 50. Sustain vaccine acceptance and demand by developing a communication and community engagement plan. 51. Hold regular press briefings and scientific discussions to promote transparency and share accurate information. 52. Engage religious, community, and opinion leaders, including medical professionals, to advocate for vaccination. 53. Proactively manage misinformation and disinformation through specialized national capacities for infodemic management. 54. Use hotlines and surveys to understand community perceptions and concerns about vaccination. 55. Create dashboards to provide real-time information to the public. 56. Utilize all media platforms, including television, radio, social media, and print media, to disseminate information effectively. 57. Establish systems for vaccine safety monitoring, including multi-disciplinary teams and digital tools for AEFI reporting and response. 58. Train and retain health workers while sensitizing vaccine recipients and their relatives to report AEFIs. 59. Deploy medical experts for on-site management of serious AEFIs.
